text:
Git branching is a powerful feature in version control that helps teams work together without stepping on each other's toes. Instead of everyone editing the main code at once, developers create feature branches for new tasks, like fixing a bug or adding a function. Each branch acts as a separate workspace where you can test ideas freely.

Once the work is complete, the next step is merging, which brings your changes back into the main branch. Before that, many teams use pull requests. This is a review step where teammates check your code, discuss improvements, and approve it. This simple workflow keeps the project clean, reduces errors, and makes collaboration smooth for everyone.
